source_acquisition.search_note: The PDF links the author repository Levi-Ackman/TeCh on p. 1 and the README title/authors match the paper. gh recursive tree inspection of TeCh main (49 entries; latest README commit 9a378cc) found no plot, figure, visual, table, LaTeX, TikZ, PGF, SVG, notebook, or style source; only four README user-attachment rasters match Figures 1–4. Figure 5, all tables, and generation parameters have no public visual source. The automated inventory selected DL4mHealth/Medformer because the paper cites it for preprocessed data/baseline code; its 83-entry tree and figs assets are for Medformer, not TeCh objects. The local corpus/visual_sources/iclr-2026-4019795d726c directory is absent.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figures use local pastel categorical palettes with black/gray structure lines; tables use black/white booktabs, dark-red best values, and (in Tables 2–3) blue underlined second-best values. Color semantics are local rather than a paper-wide method/uncertainty scale.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: All five figure bodies are embedded RGB JPEG rasters on PDF pages 2, 4, 5, 8, and 10. Captions, equations, table text, and table rules are native PDF text/vector objects; raster labels and dense table values drive small-size risk.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L and Computer Modern math are stable in native text, while raster figures use sans-serif-like labels and independent pastel palettes. Booktabs rules and bold-best conventions recur, but table typography varies from readable metadata to very small multi-metric appendix grids.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: (a): Illustration of Temporal dependencies within each channel, and channel dependencies across channels. (b): Interaction between channels in EEG/ECG signals is centrally controlled by the brain/heart. (c): Attention module is a decentralized structure, where each token attends to all other tokens equally. (d): The proposed Core Token Aggregation-Redistribution (CoTAR) module operates in a centralized manner, with a core token as a proxy.

color.semantic_mapping: EEG/ECG trace, biological-source, token, and explanatory-text roles are local categorical encodings; panel position and labels also carry the contrast.

encodings.x: panel sequence and local temporal/channel direction
encodings.shape: signal traces, token boxes, brain/heart icons, and arrows
encodings.text: direct panel labels and explanatory phrases

figures.data_and_statistics: Mechanism illustration only; no sample, unit, aggregation, denominator, uncertainty, or failure values. Panels (c) and (d) show three token nodes and directed paths; panel (b) shows three channels around a brain/heart proxy.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction centralized-biological-source claim (p. 2) → Figure 1(b) versus decentralized attention (c) → CoTAR proxy (d) → §4.1 Figure 2/Eqs. (1)–(2) → Figure 4(a) resource comparison and Tables 5/8 CoTAR ablation.
design_strengths: Same visual vocabulary makes the biological source, attention graph, and core-token proxy comparable.
Direct labels eliminate a legend.
Arrow, shape, and color cues make the conceptual contrast fast to scan.
design_weaknesses: Small italic annotations and pastel colors lose contrast in grayscale or at print size.
The panels omit equations, dimensions, and aggregation weights that determine the module.
The biological illustration can read as analogy rather than measured evidence.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use matched baseline/proposed panels at one abstraction level, with direct arrows and explicit role labels, before introducing formal equations.

evidence.label: p. 2 §1 Introduction / Figure 1 panels (a)–(d), centralized biological source versus attention/CoTAR

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Illustration of attention and Core Token Aggregation-Redistribution (CoTAR). Attention is organized in a decentralized way where each token directly interacts with all tokens, introducing a Quadratic complexity. CoTAR first aggregates a core token and then redistributes it across channels to facilitate centralized channel interaction, bringing only Linear complexity.

color.semantic_mapping: Pale panel fills distinguish Attention from CoTAR; colored token/tensor blocks mark local components.

encodings.shape: rounded operation boxes, matrices, and arrows

figures.data_and_statistics: Analytic mechanism diagram, not an empirical plot. It depicts token interaction as O(S²) for Attention and O(S) for CoTAR, with three illustrative token positions; no sample, variance, or measured resource quantity.
figures.evidence_relation: §4.1 attention/CoTAR mechanism and Eqs. (1)–(2) → Figure 2 operation sequence → Algorithm 1 (p. 19) → Figure 4(a) APAVA efficiency and Tables 5/8 CoTAR ablations.
design_strengths: Paired panels keep both methods at the same operation level.
Complexity labels and flow order make the replacement understandable before Eq. (2).
Direct labels avoid legend decoding.
design_weaknesses: Matrix/tensor icons are schematic and do not show dimensions or the softmax axis.
Pale fills and tiny operation text are raster-dependent.
The complexity claim is theoretical rather than tied to a measured curve in the figure.
figures.reusable_pattern: Place baseline and replacement pipelines side by side, preserve operation order, and annotate the complexity change where the data-flow structure changes.

evidence.label: p. 4 §4.1 / Figure 2, attention versus CoTAR operation flow

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Overview of TeCh. MedTS signals X ∈ R^{T×C} are embedded into Temporal embedding and Channel embedding. Then, each embedding is processed using Transformer encoders, with attention replaced by CoTAR. The final output representation from each branch is averaged across channels and added, then projected to the final predicted logits Ŷ ∈ R^K.

color.semantic_mapping: Teal upper Temporal and salmon/orange lower Channel branch, with gray intermediate modules and black flow structure.

encodings.y: Temporal top branch versus Channel bottom branch
encodings.shape: signal traces, embedding blocks, encoder stack, average/plus/projection boxes
encodings.facet: two parallel branches within one architecture
encodings.text: dimensions, ×M/×N, operation names, and output notation

figures.data_and_statistics: Architecture only. Input X ∈ R^{T×C} is mapped to E ∈ R^{P×D} and H ∈ R^{C×D}; averaged branch outputs are fused and projected to logits. No dataset sample, performance, uncertainty, or failure value is encoded.
figures.evidence_relation: §4.2 Adaptive Dual Tokenization and Eqs. (3)–(5) → Figure 3 pipeline → Tables 4/7 tokenization ablation → Tables 2/3 main comparisons.
design_strengths: Parallel branches and the explicit fusion node expose the adaptive design.
Dimensions and ×M/×N labels connect the image to equations.
The architecture is readable without a separate legend.
design_weaknesses: Many small labels compete with the central encoder block.
The diagram does not show exact averaging placement or all CoTAR tensor dimensions.
Branch colors are weakened in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Show parallel alternatives with identical visual grammar, annotate branch-specific repetition, and make the fusion operator an explicit node.

evidence.label: p. 5 §4.2 / Figure 3, TeCh temporal/channel branches and fusion

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4: (a): Efficiency and Effectiveness analysis of TeCh and other baselines on APAVA dataset with batch size B = 128. ‘#’ stands for ‘former’ to save space. (b): Robustness of attention and CoTAR to noise when using Channel or Temporal embedding. We consistently increase the intensity β (the standard deviation) of Gaussian random noise from 0.0 to 20.0 on the last channel of the PTB dataset. F1-Score is used to quantify the change.

color.semantic_mapping: Panel (a) uses local method colors for labeled bubbles; panel (b) maps four colors to Channel/Temporal × CoTAR/Attention curves.

encodings.x: inference time in milliseconds (a) and noise level β (b)
encodings.text: direct method labels, # abbreviation, and MB bubble-size key

figures.data_and_statistics: Panel (a) compares APAVA B=128 accuracy against inference time and bubble-encoded memory (100–900 MB key). Panel (b) adds Gaussian noise of standard deviation β to the PTB last channel from 0.0 to 20.0 and plots F1 at six levels for Channel/Temporal Attention/CoTAR. No error bars, bands, repeats, or failure values are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: §5.3 resource claim and robustness setup (p. 8) → panel (a) supports the TeCh memory/time comparison → panel (b) tests the centralized-noise rationale → Table 5/8 CoTAR ablations and Tables 2/3 main results.
design_strengths: Combines cost and robustness in one compact object.
Panel (a) exposes a three-variable trade-off using position, bubble area, and direct labels.
Panel (b) uses shared x levels and marker-coded series for trend comparison.
design_weaknesses: Memory measurement protocol and timing repetitions are not encoded.
No uncertainty display makes close curves look more certain than documented.
The two panels use different y metrics and the legend is attached only to panel (b).
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a resource trade-off scatter with a controlled perturbation curve, and state measurement repetitions and uncertainty in the caption or adjacent text.

evidence.label: p. 8 §5.3 / Figure 4 panels (a)–(b), APAVA resource and PTB noise tests

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5: T-SNE visualization of the core token generated by CoTAR and other tokens. We visualize the embedding space of both temporal and channel.

color.semantic_mapping: Red hexagon denotes Core Token; blue circle denotes Others, with row/column labels defining embedding space and dataset.

encodings.text: dataset titles, Temporal/Channel row labels, and shared legend

figures.data_and_statistics: Qualitative t-SNE projection of learned embeddings for ADFTD, APAVA, and PTB in Temporal and Channel spaces. One red hexagonal Core Token and many blue circular other tokens appear per panel; no sample rule, perplexity, seed, axis units, uncertainty, or repeated projections are reported in the caption.
figures.evidence_relation: §5.4 core-token central-position claim → six-panel visual check → latent physiological-state interpretation → Appendix C.6 Table 11 centralization diagnostics. The figure supplies qualitative evidence only; no supervised probe or intervention closes the interpretability claim.
design_strengths: Shared row/column scaffold supports cross-dataset scanning.
Shape redundancy preserves the core/other distinction.
Both tokenization spaces align with the dual-branch architecture.
design_weaknesses: Unlabeled t-SNE axes and missing projection protocol prevent reproducibility.
Point density and centrality are suggestive but not quantified.
The caption omits the color/shape key and panel mapping.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a stable row/column matrix and shared legend for qualitative representation checks, while reporting the embedding protocol and a quantitative summary alongside it.

(ii) Temporal: Only Temporal embedding is used. (iii) Channel: Only Channel embedding is used. (iv) Dual: Both Temporal and Channel embedding are used. The best is Bolded

tables.uncertainty: Accuracy and F1-Score cells show mean ± standard deviation from the five-seed protocol; the caption defines interventions but not the ± notation.

Variant descriptions make the intervention explicit.

design_weaknesses: Long methods caption sits above a compressed table.

No uncertainty definition or per-column direction is given; red-only highlighting is color-led.
tables.reusable_pattern: Place a controlled-variant matrix under a two-level dataset×metric header, define the intervention in the caption, and provide a full-data appendix expansion.

tables.label: Table 11

caption.text: Table 11: Quantitative comparison of the centralized property. We measure centralization using: (1) Spectral Centralization Index (SCI), the ratio of the largest eigenvalue to total variance, and (2) Dynamic Influence Centralization (DIC), the normalized out-strength imbalance of a first-order VAR model. Higher values indicate stronger centralized behavior.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty or replicate summary; one SCI and one DIC scalar is shown per dataset.
tables.data_and_statistics: Two metric rows (SCI, DIC) compare eight datasets grouped under EEG, ECG, Energy, and Climate; values are printed to three decimal places.

design_strengths: Hierarchical signal-family headers make the intended contrast explicit.
Caption defines both metrics and their direction.
Moderate width and three-decimal precision remain readable.
design_weaknesses: One scalar per dataset hides subject/sampling variation.
No uncertainty or statistical comparison accompanies prose saying “significantly higher”.
VAR estimation choices are not exposed beyond first-order wording.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use hierarchical domain headers and define a diagnostic metric plus direction in the caption when connecting architecture motivation to data properties.

evidence.label: p. 21 Appendix C.6 / Table 11, centralization diagnostic

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 motivates centralized versus decentralized interaction; Figure 2 gives the CoTAR interface; Figure 3 gives the TeCh pipeline; Tables 1–3 establish datasets and headline comparisons; Tables 4–5 isolate tokenization and CoTAR; Figure 4 tests efficiency and noise robustness; Figure 5 gives qualitative core-token geometry; Tables 6–12 extend settings, ablations, related models, cross-validation, centralization, and MedGNN comparison.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Every object begins with Figure/Table n:. Figure 3 uses a bold overview title; Tables 2–5 and 7–8 combine setup, intervention definitions, and highlighting rules in long captions. Figure 4 best specifies perturbation and encoding, while Figure 5 omits the key and protocol.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Table 1/2/3 use a single metric-header row; ablation and comparison tables use dataset groups over Accuracy/F1-Score; Table 11 adds signal-family groups over dataset names. Dataset/metric order is stable across main and appendix evidence.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figures 1–3 and Algorithm 1 supply the concept/method interface; Tables 2/3 are headline comparisons; Tables 4/5 isolate tokenization and CoTAR; Figure 4 adds resource/robustness evidence; Figure 5 is qualitative; Tables 7/8 expand the ablations.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Appendix Table 6 supplies hyperparameters; Tables 7/8 expand main ablations; Table 9 contextualizes related backbones; Table 10 tests subject-ID split sensitivity; Table 11 diagnoses centralization; Table 12 adds MedGNN. No appendix Figure calibrates Figure 5.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Native text is coherent Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern, but raster figures use a separate sans-serif-like language and dense tables shrink numeric text to approximately 4–6 pt. Caption size is stable while object text is not.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Pastel colors are reused only within individual figures. Main Tables 2/3 use red best and blue underlined second-best values; most other tables use red best only or grayscale. No cross-object color key exists, so labels, shape, and typography carry global linkage.

most_reusable_patterns: Parallel branch pipeline with explicit fusion (Figure 3).
Stable dataset×metric headers across main, ablation, and appendix tables.
Paired cost/perturbation views in one figure (Figure 4).
Hierarchical domain headers with metric definitions for a mechanism diagnostic (Table 11).
highest_value_objects: Figure 2 for the method operation-level interface.
Table 2 for the headline multi-metric comparison.
Tables 4 and 5 for separable tokenization/CoTAR interventions.
Figure 4 for the combined efficiency/robustness visual.
Table 11 for connecting the centralization premise to dataset diagnostics.
failure_patterns: Captions overloaded with intervention prose but missing ±/aggregation definitions.
Color-dependent highlighting without a robust grayscale equivalent.
Figure 4 resource claims without a visible measurement protocol.
Figure 5 qualitative centrality claims without axes, t-SNE parameters, uncertainty, or quantitative centrality summary.
Public source limited to four README raster attachments with no plot/table generators.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Make the centralized-versus-decentralized mechanism explicit with matched diagrams, preserve a stable dataset×metric table grammar for results and ablations, and pair every qualitative or efficiency claim with a reproducible protocol and uncertainty-bearing quantitative view.
